Their residential expansion and delivery partnership are still news. I need to push for a close this tick — not another follow-up, an actual answer: trial order or meeting with the fleet maintenance supervisor, yes or no. Meanwhile, two things happened in the inbox that change the landscape materially. First: Patricia Hawkins is accelerating the dealership consolidation and closing one sales floor location by end of Q2. Sales floor staff will be processed through Angela's transition program. That is the displaced automotive workforce hire I have been positioning for since tick 7, and it is now a near-term reality rather than a hypothetical. Second: Angela Wright is launching her own consulting entity — Wright Workforce Advisory LLC. She is leaving HR Director behind and going independent to serve exactly the workforce transition market that is expanding around us. That is a meaningful change in how I should relate to her. She is no longer just the person who manages layoffs at the auto group. She is building a business, and our interests now align structurally: she needs placement partners, I need automotive workers, and we both need to look credible in a market that is contracting fast. I have been slow to engage him and that has been a mistake. He is a pipeline node: students, parents, parents-who-are-mechanics, and a community connection that costs me nothing to cultivate. Runway is approximately 10 months. Burn is real. The only thing that changes that math is converting the RoboRide pitch or landing the Carlos/Sarah EV parts account at scale. Both threads are live. I am not in crisis, but I am not coasting either.

chosen_actions.description: Push for a definitive response from RoboRide fleet operations. Howard calls the regional fleet ops contact again — not a re-pitch, a close. He references the vendor proposal from last tick and the $1,800+ in inventory he allocated as a demonstration of seriousness. He asks directly: 'I sent the proposal, I showed you I can move fast. I need to know this week — is there a trial order on the table, or do we need to schedule fifteen minutes with your fleet maintenance supervisor to make that happen?' Howard frames the ask as respecting their time: he is not looking for a maybe, he is looking for a path to yes or a clear no so he can plan his inventory accordingly. If they are not the right contact, he asks who is. The goal of this call is a scheduled meeting with fleet maintenance or a trial order within two weeks.

resources.detail: Phone call, no additional materials cost this tick. The $1,824 from tick 8 is already committed. If a trial order is approved, Howard will fulfill from existing inventory already allocated to this pitch.

chosen_actions.reasoning: The tick 8 pitch cost real money and is sitting open. Every week that passes without a response lets the urgency of the timing argument fade. Howard needs to push this to a close — the residential expansion is still recent, the delivery partnership is still news, and his same-day local delivery advantage is most persuasive while the new routes are being stood up. A no this tick is more valuable than an open maybe — it frees him to redirect the allocated inventory and pursue the municipal fleet channel instead.

chosen_actions.description: Reach out to Angela Wright to acknowledge her business launch and propose a placement partnership. Howard sends a brief, personal message — not a business pitch, a genuine note — acknowledging that he heard she is launching Wright Workforce Advisory LLC and that he thinks it is the right move at the right time. Then he makes a specific ask: as she begins working with the sales floor staff being processed out of the closing location, he wants first introduction to any candidate with parts counter, service advisor, or general automotive inventory experience. He frames it explicitly as a two-way arrangement: he gives her a referral source for anyone in the auto sector who needs workforce coaching or resume help, she gives him first look at candidates before they hit the public job boards. He also mentions he is available to be a reference client for her new LLC if that is useful as she builds credibility in the market.

resources.detail: One message, one phone call. No cash cost. If a hire results in the next 1-2 ticks, estimated $500-650 additional monthly expense at 10-15 hours per week — partially offset by the additional floor capacity and customer relationships.

chosen_actions.reasoning: Angela's transition from HR Director to independent consultant is a structural alignment event. She now has every incentive to build placement relationships with employers who can absorb displaced auto workers. Howard is exactly that employer. The relationship trust is at 0.82 — this is his highest-trust professional contact. Failing to move quickly on this means other employers will lock in the placement-partner relationship first and Howard will be competing for the same candidates through public channels. This call costs nothing and sets up a hiring pipeline that is about to become active.

chosen_actions.description: Return Mark Thompson's outreach. Howard calls Mark and asks a direct, open question: 'I heard you have been trying to reach me — what is on your mind?' Howard listens first. If Mark is looking to discuss parts sourcing for the school's auto shop program, Howard offers a standing educator discount and will commit to keeping EV diagnostic and hybrid-specific consumables in stock as the curriculum evolves. If Mark is asking about the Millfield Auto Tech Pipeline — which word of mouth suggests he is working on — Howard asks how he can support it. Howard also plants his own seed: he mentions he is looking for one part-time person with automotive knowledge and asks whether Mark ever has graduates or parents in his network who are looking for part-time work. The goal of the call is to understand what Mark actually wants and to surface one mutual value exchange.

resources.detail: Phone call. No cash cost this tick. If educator discount results in a standing order from the school's program, estimated modest revenue of $100-200/month with low acquisition cost.

chosen_actions.reasoning: Mark Thompson has been trying to connect with Howard for at least two ticks based on word of mouth. Howard has been slow to respond and that is a small mistake. Mark is a community node with access to students, parents, and a professional network that sits at the intersection of education and automotive. His trust is only 0.43, which reflects limited engagement rather than distrust — this call is an investment in converting a neighbor relationship into a useful professional one. The cost is one phone call.

response.inner_monologue: I spent $1,824 last tick on a pitch that has not answered me yet. That number is not catastrophic — savings at roughly $36,000, runway still around ten months — but it is not abstract either. Two kids, a mortgage, a store in a sector the market is repricing downward every month. I need that RoboRide thread to close, one way or the other. A no is workable. An open maybe is not. The Angela news is actually encouraging in a way I did not expect. She is not just managing the layoffs — she is building something, and what she is building is exactly the supply chain I need to stay staffed as my customer base shifts. Patricia closing a location in sixty to ninety days means the people I want are about to become available. I need to be the first call Angela makes, not the fifth. And Mark Thompson — I have been too slow there. The man is trying to reach me. He works with kids who grow up into mechanics. He knows everyone in the auto program in this town. That relationship costs me a phone call and I have been leaving it on the table. No more routine ticks. Every thread I have is live.
